issue.title: dedupe.ts misses overlapping days when two statements are uploaded together
issue.body:
Duplicate detection in `src/ingest/dedupe.ts` doesn't handle overlapping
statements uploaded together. I uploaded our September and October statements
straight after each other; both contain 28 to 30 September, and those three
days are now in the ledger twice (both uploads say 0 duplicates). On our test
account I uploaded the same two files a few minutes apart, and the second one
reported 9 duplicates, as it should. So dedupe.ts must be missing a case.
## Discussion

### ben-ops (maintainer) · 2026-11-12
Thanks. Roughly how long was there between the two uploads, and how big are
the files?

### recon-team-milan · 2026-11-12
About ten seconds apart, around 2,000 rows each. Both had finished importing
within a minute.

input.title: Serialise dedupe and insert per account so concurrent uploads see each other
input.body:
File: src/ingest/worker.ts

processJob reads existing transactions (listInRange), dedupes against them, then inserts. Two uploads for the same account can run in parallel: claimNext in src/ingest/queue.ts locks only the import_jobs row and releases it at commit, so neither job sees the other's rows and both report 0 duplicates.

Proposed change: wrap the existing-read, dedupe and insert in one transaction that takes a per-account lock first (for example pg_advisory_xact_lock keyed on the account id), so jobs for the same account run one at a time. Jobs for different accounts stay concurrent.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The dedupe logic is correct within one file, but processJob reads existing rows, dedupes and inserts with no per-account lock. claimNext in src/ingest/queue.ts locks only the job row and releases it at once, so two uploads for the same account can run in parallel and each misses the other's rows. That fits the report: about ten seconds apart, both finished, 0 duplicates. A draft pull request (pr-46) proposes serialising the read-dedupe-insert per account.
